questions: If a file name matches the pattern but a file with the same name already exists in the target directory, should the function overwrite it, skip it, raise an error, or something else?
Should the function preserve the directory structure from the source when moving files, or flatten all matched files directly into the target directory?
Does 'matching a substring' mean the pattern is applied to the full file path (including directories) or only the base file name?
Should the function follow symbolic links when traversing the source directory, or treat them as files/directories to skip?
If the target directory is created, should its parent directories also be created if they don't exist, or should the function fail?
Should the function move only regular files, or also other types like directories or special files that match the pattern?
If moving a file fails (e.g., permission error), should the function abort and return count so far, continue skipping that file, or raise an exception?
Is the pattern matching case-sensitive or case-insensitive by default?
